prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire flat bands

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the case where a simple, universal mechanism (moire interference flattening the bands at a particular twist angle) was written down as a clean continuum model by Bistritzer and MacDonald in 2011 and then confirmed in a striking way in 2018, when Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity at the predicted angle. This is the model-first, mechanism-first discovery I trust most. It has been reproduced by many independent groups, the flat-band picture has stayed stable, and it has opened a field of tunable correlated quantum matter in which one can vary carrier density and twist angle in a single device. Theory and experiment are cleanly paired, so a three-name prize is natural.
statement.case_against: The microscopic origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated insulators are still debated, twist-angle disorder limits sample reproducibility, and the experimental discovery was made by a team in which the first author (Yuan Cao) and other junior members cannot be credited under the three-person limit. The discovery is only eight years old, whereas B036 (optical lattice clocks) is older, better settled and has broad support among colleagues, so the maturity objection to B022 is a serious one.

responses.point: Johansson ranked B022 last of his shortlisted entries and argued that the discovery is recent, the superconducting mechanism is unresolved, and a robust consensus would justify waiting; he preferred older, more settled candidates.
responses.response: I accept that the pairing mechanism is open, but I would separate the discovery from the mechanism. What is being credited is the magic-angle flat band and the existence of correlated and superconducting phases in it, and that part has been confirmed by many groups for years. Waiting for the pairing mechanism would be an unusually strict test, since for the cuprates and for the quantum Hall effects the discovery was recognised long before the mechanism was understood. I do agree that this is the weakest point of my choice, and I would shift my view if the committee finds that the flat-band picture is itself being contested.

responses.point: Eriksson ranked B054 (topological insulators) first and B022 second, and judged B022 original and highly Nobel-worthy but preferred the cleaner two-person theory-plus-experiment split of MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, noting that Bistritzer is a legitimate co-theorist.
responses.response: I take Eriksson's support for B022 seriously and we agree on its scientific standing. I would keep Bistritzer, because the continuum model is a joint paper and the magic angle comes out of exactly that calculation, so dropping him would misattribute the central theoretical idea. On B054 I disagree that it should lead. Its credited trio omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who predicted the HgTe effect, and the 3D topological-insulator discoverers, so any allocation is contestable, and the 2016 prize already covered the conceptual ground of topological phases. B022 has the cleaner attribution on the supplied names.

responses.point: Kroll ranked B036 first as the clearest instance of a new measurement technique, mature and reproduced in many laboratories, with a clean Katori-Ye allocation and the redefinition of the second pending.
responses.response: I agree that B036 is the safest option on maturity and attribution, and it is my first alternative. My reservation is that it extends a line already recognised in 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (ion-trap control), so the incremental case needs to be made, and Kroll himself lists priority among several clock groups and the timing of the SI redefinition as open. If the committee wants a prize whose scientific content is a new mechanism rather than a very large improvement in precision, B022 is the better choice. If the committee weighs maturity above all, I would be comfortable moving to B036.

responses.point: Olsson ranked B021 (aberration correction) first, B036 second and B022 third, and flagged that the junior experimentalists of the 2018 twisted-graphene papers (Cao, Fatemi) cannot be named, and that earlier twisted-graphene theory could be claimed as precursors.
responses.response: Both points are fair and I regard them as real limits on the allocation rather than reasons to drop the candidate. The three-person rule always excludes junior authors, and the group leader who conceived and ran the experiment is the established pattern. On precursors, Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto computed moire bands earlier, but the specific magic-angle flat-band condition and its link to a strongly correlated regime come from Bistritzer and MacDonald. I would ask the committee to check that archival question rather than assume it. I also note that B021 has only one supporter in the opening round and an acknowledged incompleteness on Knut Urban, so I cannot support it as a lead.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the unresolved superconducting pairing mechanism as a barrier to recognition at this stage.
Exact priority of the magic-angle flat-band result relative to earlier moire band theory by other authors.
Whether the three-person limit adequately represents the experimental team behind the 2018 observations.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. I have no known collaboration with any candidate on the shortlist. I work in the same Gothenburg physics environment as colleagues Goran Johansson and Eva Olsson, but no specific collaboration with them is documented and it does not bear on any shortlisted candidate.
